plan.thinking: First round: no results yet. The constant construction gives only R=2/3. Exact hand calculation for the symmetric bump h=[1,2,1] gives R=196/288≈0.68056, suggesting peaked unimodal shapes beat the flat start. I will use the deepen slot to optimize step heights from the constant start, and two explores: one over smooth parametric bumps, one over evolutionary search for small-support shapes. Threads: one on the best line (local height optimization), one off it (shape discovery).
plan.gist: Constant gives 2/3; peaked bumps may exceed it. Schedule local height optimization from p0001 plus smooth-bump and evolutionary shape searches.

beliefs.statement: The constant step function with 50 equal heights has R = 2/3 exactly.
beliefs.why: p0001 scores 0.666667 with a constant array.

beliefs.statement: A symmetric peaked step shape such as h=[1,2,1] exceeds the constant value: exact evaluation gives R≈0.68056.
beliefs.refuted_if: An exact run of [1,2,1] or its scaled/padded version scores at or below 2/3.
beliefs.why: Direct computation of the piecewise-linear convolution formula gives 196/288.

beliefs.statement: Peaked unimodal h makes f*f less triangular and relatively fuller near its maximum, increasing ||f*f||_2^2 relative to ||f*f||_inf while keeping ||f*f||_1 fixed.
beliefs.refuted_if: Optimization finds that flat or U-shaped h systematically beats all peaked unimodal shapes.

beliefs.statement: The best shapes are symmetric unimodal bumps; sparse multi-spike or highly asymmetric shapes score below the best smooth bump.
beliefs.refuted_if: A sparse or asymmetric construction scores higher than the best unimodal bump found.
beliefs.why: Smooth bumps already beat constant; isolated spikes appear penalized by the 2/3 knot factor.

agenda.question: What step-height profile maximizes R when starting from the constant best line, and can local height optimization find a peaked bump?
agenda.plan: Run a stochastic hill-climb/memetic search on 50-200 heights initialized from p0001's constant array; if it gains, refine the best profile with more mutations and smoothing; if not, test a direct [1,2,1]-style bump.
agenda.stop: Close after 3 experiments without a real gain over 0.666667.
agenda.why: The best line is constant and must be improved directly.

agenda.question: Which parametric or discovered shape family gives the largest R, and what qualitative shape does it have?
agenda.plan: Explore a smooth power-exponential bump family and an evolutionary search over small-support heights; if either beats 0.68, branch to refine its best shape and scale it to larger N.
agenda.stop: Close after 3 experiments without a real gain over the best known R.
agenda.why: Shape discovery off the best line may reveal a better construction class.

experiments.hypothesis: Local stochastic optimization of the step heights, initialized from the constant start, will find a peaked bump and improve R above 2/3.
experiments.change: In construct, initialize h from start if given (otherwise ones(50)). Run a memetic hill-climb for about 28 s of CPU: repeatedly mutate h (multiplicative lognormal perturbations, additive noise, local smoothing, occasional zeroing, renormalization), accept improvements in exact R, keep a population of several candidates, and periodically restart from a Gaussian bump with random width. Return the best h found.
experiments.if_gain: Use the best profile as the new start for a second deepen experiment with finer local mutations and larger N.
experiments.if_not: Test a direct parameterized [1,2,1]-style bump and investigate whether the optimizer is stuck due to initialization.

experiments.hypothesis: A symmetric power-exponential bump family contains shapes with R substantially above 2/3.
experiments.change: From scratch, set N=201 and construct h_i = exp(-(|i-c|/sigma)^p) for i=0..N-1, with c=(N-1)/2. Search over sigma in [1,80] and p in [1,4] using a coarse grid plus local refinement, evaluating exact R for each candidate. Return the best h.
experiments.prediction: Best R > 0.68, with an optimal p around 2 (Gaussian-like) and moderate sigma.
experiments.if_gain: Refine sigma and p near the optimum, then try asymmetric or multi-parameter bump families.
experiments.if_not: Conclude that smooth parametric bumps are insufficient and focus on evolutionary shape discovery.

experiments.hypothesis: Evolutionary search over small-support nonnegative height arrays will discover a better qualitative shape than simple parametric families.
experiments.change: From scratch, run a genetic/evolutionary search over N=21 heights: initialize a population with random positive arrays and some structured bumps ([1,2,1], binomial, Gaussian); mutate entries multiplicatively/additively, include crossover and occasional zeroing, select by exact R, and run until the CPU budget. Return the best array, optionally padded with zeros to N=101.
experiments.prediction: Best R > 0.68, possibly revealing a binomial-like or smooth peak profile.
experiments.if_gain: Scale and refine the discovered profile to N up to 200 and test local perturbations.
experiments.if_not: Conclude that small-support evolutionary search is too noisy and rely on parametric/local optimization.

came_back.note: Memetic search from constant reached 0.840412, far above 2/3; peaked dense bump.
Power-exponential bump reached 0.723364 > 0.68, but parametric family is limited.
Evolved 21-step dense bump (padded) reached 0.828911 > 0.68; coarser than p0003.

plan.thinking: Both lines converge on dense, moderately peaked bumps: p0003 (N=50) 0.8404 beats p0005 (N=21) 0.8289, and parametric p0004 (0.723) is far behind free-form search. So free-form optimization + higher resolution is the main lever. p0003 is asymmetric (peak at 0.65) with ~12% zeros, so 'symmetric' is not required. I will (1) refine p0003 multiscale to N=100-200, (2) run basin-hopping/structural moves to test whether 0.8404 is a strong local optimum or a different structure (gaps/multi-hump) wins, and (3) branch from p0005 with a population search at higher N to see if its basin competes. Keep threads A1 (main line), A2 (shape family), new n1 (structural features).
plan.gist: Free-form dense bumps win (p0003 0.8404 > p0005 0.8289 > parametric 0.723); push p0003 to higher resolution and test structural alternatives, plus refine the p0005 branch.

beliefs.statement: Peaked non-flat shapes substantially exceed 2/3: free-form optimized bumps reach 0.72-0.84, versus 2/3 for the constant.
beliefs.why: Three independent constructions all beat 2/3 by large margins.

beliefs.statement: A peaked (non-flat) f makes f*f fuller near its maximum relative to ||f*f||_inf, raising R while ||f*f||_1 is fixed by scaling.
beliefs.why: The best shapes are peaked bumps, not flat; consistent with the mechanism.

beliefs.statement: The best shape is an asymmetric dense bump with a few zero steps (p0003 peak at 0.65 of support, ~12% zeros), not a symmetric unimodal profile.
beliefs.why: p0003 is clearly asymmetric yet is the best found, contradicting the old 'symmetric' claim.

beliefs.statement: Higher step resolution improves R: N=50 (0.8404) beats N=21 (0.8289), so refining the best shape to N>=100 can exceed 0.85.
beliefs.refuted_if: Multiscale refinement of p0003 at N=100-200 fails to beat 0.8404.
beliefs.why: Suggests resolution, not just basin, is a lever.

beliefs.statement: The optimum is a single dense asymmetric bump, not a sparse multi-spike comb or difference-set construction.
beliefs.refuted_if: A comb/difference-set or strongly multi-hump construction scores above the best dense bump.
beliefs.why: Both winning shapes are dense bumps; worth testing directly.

agenda.plan: Refine p0003 multiscale: polish at N=50, then linearly upsample to N=100 and N=200 and re-optimize each with local search, keeping the global best. If it gains, push resolution further and make it the new base; if not, resolution is saturated at N=50.
agenda.why: p0003 is the best line and higher resolution is the untested lever.

agenda.question: What structural features (asymmetry, zero gaps, number of humps) characterize the best shape, and is p0003 a strong local optimum?
agenda.plan: Run basin-hopping/annealing from p0003 with large structural moves (zero blocks, split/merge humps) plus local refinement; if a structurally different shape beats 0.8404, adopt its features; if not, conclude 0.8404 is a robust local optimum.
agenda.stop: 3 experiments without a real gain over 0.8404.
agenda.why: Tests whether the dense-bump local optimum is global or whether gaps/multi-hump structure helps.

agenda.plan: Branch from p0005: refine its construction at higher resolution with a population/genetic search (crossover + multiplicative mutation + local polish), compare its basin to p0003's. If it gains, keep the line alive; if not, deprioritize it.
agenda.why: p0005 is the best of a separate line; let it mature at higher N.

experiments.hypothesis: Finer step resolution lets the best dense bump reach higher R.
experiments.change: Load start (p0003's 50 heights). Polish at N=50 with coordinate-descent + small adjacent-entry perturbations for a few seconds; then linearly upsample the best array to N=100 and re-optimize, then to N=200 and re-optimize, keeping the global best. Exact scoring via np.convolve; use the full budget with a safe margin.
experiments.if_gain: Push to N=200 (or higher) and make the refined shape the new base for the main line.
experiments.if_not: Resolution is saturated at N=50; shift effort to structural changes.

experiments.hypothesis: p0003 may be a strong local optimum; larger structural moves (gaps, multi-hump) could find a better basin.
experiments.change: From p0003, run a basin-hopping/simulated-annealing search at N=50-80 with large structural moves (zero out blocks, split/merge humps, big multiplicative jumps) interleaved with local refinement, accepting uphill moves with a decreasing temperature, keeping the global best.
experiments.prediction: Either no gain (0.8404 is a robust local optimum) or a structurally different shape scoring > 0.845.
experiments.if_gain: Record the winning structural feature and test it on the main line.
experiments.if_not: Conclude the dense bump is a robust local optimum; focus on resolution and fine-tuning.

experiments.hypothesis: The p0005 basin can match or beat p0003 when refined at higher resolution with a population search.
experiments.change: Take p0005's array (N=101), upsample to N=150, and run a genetic algorithm (population ~40, crossover + multiplicative mutation + local polish) for the full budget, keeping the best. Compare the resulting shape and R to p0003.
experiments.prediction: Reaches >= 0.83; possibly >= 0.84 if the basin is competitive.
experiments.if_gain: If it beats p0003, adopt as new best and continue the branch; else compare shapes for insight.
experiments.if_not: p0005's basin is inferior; deprioritize this line.

came_back.note: Gained (+0.00045) but far short of predicted 0.845; upsampling to N=100/200 gave no gain in its own stage lines.
No real change (+0.000004): large structural moves from p0003 find nothing better, so p0003 is a strong local optimum.
p0005 basin refined to 0.8278, a loss; sparse p0005 line is clearly inferior to the dense bump.

plan.thinking: Gains have collapsed to <0.001 per 30 s; random-mutation/memetic search saturates near 0.841. p0013 (memoryless) is now best at 0.841166 with N=100 and its f*f peaks at 0.500 of support, hinting the best shape may be near-symmetric (unlike p0003's 0.65). So I will (1) try two genuinely different local mechanisms on p0013 — numerical-gradient projected ascent and exact block-coordinate line search — and (2) use the challenge slot to test whether forcing symmetry is as good as the asymmetric best, which would refute B4 and simplify the search. p0005 line is dead; park A2.
plan.gist: Random search saturates ~0.841; p0013 looks near-symmetric. Try gradient ascent and exact coordinate line search on p0013, and challenge B4 by symmetrizing p0013.

beliefs.statement: The best shape is a dense bump with a few zero steps; whether it is asymmetric is now unclear: early best p0003 peaked at 0.65 of support, but current best p0013 has its f*f maximum at 0.500 of support, suggesting a near-symmetric profile.
beliefs.why: p0013's autoconvolution peak at center is a hint of symmetry, contradicting the earlier asymmetric reading.

beliefs.statement: Higher resolution gives only small gains: N=50 -> 0.8409, N=100 -> 0.8412, and p0010's upsampling to N=200 gave no further gain. Resolution is near-saturated; N>=100 will not reach 0.85.
beliefs.why: p0010's stage lines show no gain at N=100/200, while p0013 at N=100 reached 0.841166; gains are tiny.

beliefs.statement: The optimum is a single dense bump, not a sparse multi-spike comb: p0011's structural moves from p0003 found nothing and p0012's sparse p0005 basin refined only to 0.8278.
beliefs.why: Both structural and sparse-basin experiments underperform the dense bump.

beliefs.statement: Random-mutation local/memetic search saturates near 0.841: the last three 30 s runs gained at most ~0.0008 each (p0010 +0.00045, p0011 +0.000004, p0013 +0.00076).
beliefs.why: Diminishing returns across independent 30 s runs indicate the local-search mechanism is exhausted.

agenda.plan: From p0013, apply numerical-gradient projected ascent at N=200 (then 400) with backtracking line search, and separately exact block-coordinate golden-section line search, keeping the global best. If either beats 0.841166, push resolution and adopt as base; if not, local polish is saturated and effort shifts to structural/parametric changes.
agenda.why: p0013 is the best and random mutation is exhausted; gradient/coordinate methods are untried mechanisms.
p0005 basin refined only to 0.8278 (p0012 loss); the sparse line is clearly inferior to the dense bump at 0.8412.

agenda.plan: Test the symmetry hypothesis: symmetrize p0013, re-optimize at N=200; if a symmetric-constrained shape matches the best, adopt a symmetric parametrization. Also, if slots allow later, test a principled two-hump/comb against the dense bump. If neither beats, the dense bump is confirmed.
agenda.why: p0013's f*f peak at 0.500 hints the optimum may be symmetric, which would change the search space.

experiments.hypothesis: Numerical-gradient projected ascent at N=200 finds a better local optimum than random mutation.
experiments.change: Load p0013 (N=100), upsample to N=200. Compute R and its numerical gradient wrt h (central differences). Run projected gradient ascent (Adam or normalized gradient with backtracking line search, nonneg projection, renormalize max to 1) for the full budget, keeping the global best; try N=400 if time permits.
experiments.if_gain: Push to N=400 and adopt as the new base for the main line.
experiments.if_not: Local polish is saturated; rely on structural/parametric changes.

experiments.hypothesis: Exact block-coordinate line search (golden-section per height) polishes better than random mutation.
experiments.change: Load p0013, upsample to N=100 (and try N=200). Sweep coordinates; for each height do a golden-section exact maximization of R over that coordinate (others fixed, nonneg), repeat sweeps until budget, keep the global best; alternate with small random restarts.
experiments.if_gain: Combine coordinate sweeps with the gradient method at N=200.
experiments.if_not: Coordinate ascent also saturates; the shape is a strong local optimum.

experiments.hypothesis: A symmetric profile is as good as the asymmetric best, refuting B4.
experiments.change: Load p0013, symmetrize h <- (h + h[::-1])/2, upsample to N=200, run local/memetic optimization for the budget, and report the best R and whether the result is symmetric.
experiments.prediction: Symmetric-constrained best reaches >= 0.8410, close to 0.841166 -> B4 refuted (symmetry is not a disadvantage).
experiments.if_gain: Adopt a symmetric parametrization and optimize at high resolution.
experiments.if_not: Asymmetry matters; keep the asymmetric search.
